summary: A local context-compression layer that sits between a coding agent and the model, shrinking what the agent sends (tool outputs, logs, files, RAG chunks) and trimming what the model writes back — without deleting anything. summary: A tool that learns a website's internal network requests and re-exposes them as operations an agent calls over HTTP, skipping browser automation entirely. Learned operations go into a shared catalog (a Cloudflare Worker stores specs and success/fail votes — it never proxies traffic; calls leave from your machine, logins stay local). author: @reporadarai
title_or_hook: Edge0: SSD-streamed MoE inference, 35B in 2.9 GB
summary: An open-source inference framework that runs a 35B-parameter MoE model with ~2.9 GiB peak active memory by memory-mapping expert weights from SSD and streaming only the experts a token needs. Three mechanisms per its docs: SSD expert offload (SafetensorsMmap + a cross-layer LRU SharedExpertCache), a trained per-layer prerouter that predicts the next token's experts one step ahead (the source of the claimed up-to-59% decode boost), and an unmerged LoRA that recovers most int4 quantization loss. Ships two checkpoints: Edge0-35B-A3B-preview (from Qwen3.5-MoE) and Edge0-8B-A1B-preview (from Ling-3.0-tiny). Measured in project material: 2.9 GiB / 20.4 tok/s for 35B vs 18.2 GiB for a fully resident int4 engine.
engine_training_value: Direct: the prerouter is trained on labeled expert-activation sequences — (context → next-token expert set) pairs. That dataset shape, and the hit-rate/throughput labels Edge0 publishes per benchmark (HumanEval, MMLU-Pro in its tables), are a template for training GSE's own "which features will matter next" routing layer. Data lives in the repo + paper; labels exist (activation traces are self-labeling).

author: @githubsignals
title_or_hook: gpu-unlock: Linux kernel module that removes GeForce tensor-core half-rate cap
summary: A Linux kernel module by Zagitta that runs from the initramfs before the stock NVIDIA driver binds the card, writes two internal speed selectors (SS0 0x88888888, SS1 0x8), performs a function-level reset, and lets the unmodified driver load — removing NVIDIA's product-segmentation cap that runs GeForce tensor cores at half rate for FP16/BF16/TF32 math with FP32 accumulation (the same silicon in RTX A-series pro cards runs full rate). Not a patched driver, not a VBIOS flash, so driver updates do not undo it. It does nothing unless gpu_unlock.targets= is on the kernel command line.
engine_training_value: Indirect but real: prefill throughput is the cost driver for running the reasoning engine's L1–L5 traces locally; a verified 25–55% prefill gain changes which local models are viable as trace generators/judges. No dataset or labels ship with the tool itself.

Its three levers, per the paper: inject learned operational micro-skills (facts/procedures distilled from finished sessions in that repo), prune …

For GSE itself: the same three-waste taxonomy (rediscovery, unused tools, failure loops) applied to reasoning-trace generation would produce (trace, waste-type, cost) rows for routing the L1–L5 tracks. author: @asharasjad
title_or_hook: ARLoop: fully-open looped transformers that reuse their own layers, with the training recipe published
summary: ARLoop is a looped transformer architecture: instead of stacking distinct layers, it repeatedly applies one shared set of layers (recurrence), and at each pass the input to a layer is built by attention over depth — the layer selectively pulls from earlier passes' intermediate representations (attention residuals) rather than receiving one merged residual stream. The paper's key finding is that a sliding window over recent depth matches or beats attending to the full history at larger recurrence depths, which caps the cost of the mechanism. The release is genuinely fully-open in the sense the post claims: training code, data-processing code, intermediate checkpoints, and final models are all published, which is exactly the part most looped-LLM releases withhold. Verified figures from …

author: @githubsignals
title_or_hook: BitDecoding FP4: native FP4 KV-cache decoding, ~2.4–3.0× serving throughput (VERIFIED, hardware-gated)
summary: An algorithm–system co-design for running an LLM's KV cache in native 4-bit floating point (NVFP4 / MXFP4) on FP4 Tensor Cores without the usual accuracy collapse. Three named mechanisms from the paper abstract: (a) Dual-Residual Query Quantization — splits the query into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; (b) Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling — prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; (c) Outlier-Aware Key Quantization — static smoothing + Hadamard rotation + scale search to suppress key outliers under token-wise scaling. The poster (@githubsignals) is a repo-drop aggregator/recreator; the origin is the paper + repo below.
engine_training_value: Indirect but real: cheaper long-context inference lowers the cost of generating training/rollout data and of running long-context reasoning over game corpora. The technique itself teaches no metric or label — the value is inference economics for the training loop, not a dataset.

summary: Worked sensitivity case for SCRACK: Bo Nix's 60+ yard TD scramble was worth +5.48 EPA on one play; his SCRACK bar value -12.25 (14th of 35 qualifying QBs); removing that single play drops him to -17.73 (22nd). One play = 5.48 EPA = 8 ranking places. Method lesson: publish SCRACK with leave-one-out range or per-play distribution, not point value.
engine_training_value: LOO check to fold into SCRACK build; same treatment applies to anytime-TD and explosive-rate stats.

title_or_hook: Week 8 Advanced Stats: Predicted Coverage Shells + Predicted Pressure
summary: Weekly model product with two pre-game predicted environment models: Predicted Coverage Shells (forecasting coverage shells defense will present, used to find tail events) and Predicted Pressure (forecasting QB pressure outcomes, player tags e.g. Dak Prescott BOOM tag in Predicted Pressure model for ARI@DAL). Derivatives: coverage-shell-adjusted TPRR matchups (Michael Wilson 4th-best vs Dallas), Dallas #1 most two-high/MOFO faced, Arizona #5 most zone, #1 most explosive pass rate allowed; Beta Sim game simulator. Sources PFF, NGS, FantasyPts. Substack verified live Oct 30 20:41 UTC, free preview read, remainder paywalled.
engine_training_value: Method worth benchmarking: predicts scheme environment before player matchups — ordering GSE weekly cycle lacks as explicit step; shell-adjusted TPRR derivative needs shell data GSE does not own.

author: @The_Coach_A
title_or_hook: Nub-Trips and the "shove" call
summary: Offenses use nub-Trips (TE alone on nub side) to make defense 'buy low' on TE side — Houston adds play-action to nub TE so secondary bites — while real stress is multiple vertical routes from Trips side. Split-field defense needs a 'shove' mechanism: Giants shove immediately, Ar'Darius Washington (24) to outside shoulder of #2 while Jason Pinnock (25) poaches #3's bender. Interpretive, not computable from play-by-play.
engine_training_value: Names defensive answer to specific offensive structure; pairs with predicted coverage shells — predicted shell is half the call, post-snap adjustment (shove) is other half.

author: @Timo_NFL
title_or_hook: The endgame simplification: tiny WP edges are still edges (thread part 1)
summary: Endgame decisions should be judged on sign of WP change, not size: moving WP from ~0 to +0.2% is an infinite relative gain and the correct call. Small edge was derived by logical deduction (enumerate what must happen for a comeback) before measurement; Benjamin Morris did full empirical version at FiveThirtyEight 10+ years ago. WP outputs carry uncertainty, so a hand-solvable simplification (60-second by-hand bound) is valuable.
engine_training_value: Two operating rules: report sign and must-happen chain, not just WP delta; keep a hand-checkable bound beside every model WP number

author: @karpathy
title_or_hook: autoresearch: the autonomous experiment loop
summary: Autonomous research harness: give a coding agent a small, real LLM training setup; agent edits ONE file (train.py), trains for fixed 5-minute budget, checks single metric (val_bpb — validation bits per byte, lower is better, vocab-independent), keeps or discards change, repeats — ~12 experiments/hour, ~100 overnight. Human never edits Python; human edits program.md, Markdown file that programs 'research org' (goals, constraints, process). Repo is three files: prepare.py (fixed; data + tokenizer + evaluation), train.py (agent-edited), program.md (human-edited). Verified at primary source: github.com/karpathy/autoresearch — public, MIT, 98,965 stars, 13,647 forks, 36 commits, created 2026-03-06. Requirements: single NVIDIA GPU (tested H100), Python 3.10+, uv. Forks for macOS, Windows, AMD.
engine_training_value: Pattern transfer, not GPU code: one mutable file, fixed time budget making experiments comparable, one scalar metric with keep/discard discipline, human programs org in Markdown — shape a GSE hyperparameter/weight-search harness should take
source_section: FD2 — @karpathy — autoresearch: the autonomous experiment loop

author: @karpathy
title_or_hook: llm-wiki: instead of RAG re-deriving knowledge per query, the LLM incrementally builds and maintains a persistent Markdown wiki
summary: Knowledge-architecture claim with working setup: durable knowledge lives in plain Markdown files user owns; LLM's job is wiki maintenance (ingest, link, update, prune) rather than per-query retrieval over raw chunks. Contrast case is RAG: re-derivation on every question, no compounding. He runs it as Obsidian plugin while LLM does bookkeeping. No repo link in captured text; setup described, not released.
engine_training_value: Confirmatory: MEMORY.md, memory tree, seen index, sweep reports are a file-over-app wiki with agent as bookkeeper; maintenance loop (update-on-ingest, prune-on-contradiction) is agent's job

title_or_hook: DeepSeek dsh-superagent prototype
summary: Proactive coding-agent system for one GitHub repo, packaged as bundle for DeepSeek Harness: listens to GitHub (and optionally Feishu); when allowed person asks for work, opens work item, executes it in agent's own session and directory, answers in original thread (e.g. with a PR). author: @tangotiger
title_or_hook: RE288 by venue+season
summary: Run-expectancy extension: baseball's RE24 (expected runs by base-out state, Palmer/Thorn, ~45 years old) expanded to RE288 — 24 base-out states × 12 ball-strike counts — now computed per venue+season with run environment varying by park and year, shipping on Savant. engine_training_value: Method transfer to GSE prediction engine: sparse-cell expectancy — GSE down/distance/score-state WP and EP surfaces have same thin-cell disease RE288 solves with semi-Markov blend; venue/weather effects belong inside expectancy surface, not bolted onto outputs

author: @geogristle
title_or_hook: F4 — Google SLEEP framework / Language Models Need Sleep (arXiv:2606.03979)
summary: Continual-learning schedule: wake phase where new information lives in fast short-term components, then periodic offline sleep phase distilling material into newly opened low-rank experts in slower memory blocks (knowledge seeding, distillation upward from small fast module into larger slower one), plus dreaming stage training on filtered self-generated samples. Vendor-reported near-perfect long-context retention to 10M tokens on BABILong and AIME 2024 79.2 for Sleep-trained Qwen3-8B vs 73.8 base; no code shipped.
engine_training_value: Architectural transfer only: scheduled consolidation passes over agent memory (distill day's raw captures into curated store, clear scratch) are SLEEP's pattern with files instead of weights.
provenance_json: "Behrouz, Hashemi, Javanmard, Mirrokni, Google Research, arXiv:2606.03979"

author: @Gorden_Sun
title_or_hook: F3 — DecisionRAG (arXiv:2610.35868)
summary: Retrieval by navigation instead of similarity search. A pretrained decision model walks a corpus hierarchy (topics, documents, sections, passages), judging all candidate branches at each level jointly in one forward pass with no tokens generated, descending only promising branches. Paper reports beating dense retrieval plus 8B reranker by 13.8 R@1 on MultiDoc2Dial and 17.4 Hit@1 on Natural Questions, 0.7-1.8s per query, including a 2.68M-paragraph Wikipedia corpus. Default decision model is commercial TypeSafe Jev; no official code release found.
engine_training_value: Transferable design: organize corpus as navigable tree and let a model prune branches level by level instead of embedding-searching a flat index; prototype could navigate lane-run-dossier tree.
provenance_json: "Chao Wan et al., Cornell, arXiv:2610.35868 'Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models'"

author: @run_the_sims
title_or_hook: W2 — The Nash correction: 55% was NOT a Nash equilibrium
summary: Public retraction and rebuild of the 55% pass Nash claim, verified by full read of Side Quest article. Defense call redefined to box advantage (Tej Seth: blockers minus defenders in box; Defense+ 34%, Even 48%, Offense+ 18% of early downs; 87,000 plays 2022-2025). Pass beats run against every box, so passing is dominant and no Nash equilibrium existed. With pass-certainty decay (pass payoff falls 0.027 EPA per 10 points certainty vs Defense+, 0.019 Even, 0.014 Offense+), peaks are 58% Defense+, 63% Even, 77% Offense+; best mix about 71%, range 56-75%, reframed as Stackelberg equilibrium.
engine_training_value: Skeleton reproducible from nflverse alone (box counts, EPA, xPass); blocker count needs SumerSports charting. Decay slopes are portable numbers matchup reasoning can cite.

author: @HowToPrompt__
title_or_hook: SwaT (Swarm Telepathy): KV-cache transfer between LLM families (MIT CSAIL)
summary: A research system, verified at secondary/primary sources: SwaT trains a small mapper that translates one frozen LLM's KV-cache into another model family's KV-cache format, so a receiving model can continue from the sender's internal state without the sender's context ever being converted to text (prefill-free handoff). The paper (arXiv 2610.15095, Alabdulkareem et al., MIT CSAIL / MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab) reports — as-reported, no independent replication found — that with cache compaction it beat text-to-text handoffs by a mean of ~40% accuracy at ~4x speed across 17 benchmarks / 12 LLMs / 6 families, and even transferred vision ability from a VLM to a text-only receiver.
engine_training_value: None for the prediction engine — context only for the fleet. Indirect: cache-handoff could move full reasoning traces between the engine's open-model workers without summary loss; no dataset or labels involved.

author: @godofwaaar
title_or_hook: The 100-Strategy Selection Trap (Monte Carlo backtest overfitting)
summary: A selection-bias demonstration with its numbers printed in the abstract: 10,000 independent Monte Carlo trials; each trial evaluates 100 independently simulated zero-alpha strategies on 60 in-sample trades, selects the best performer, then evaluates that winner on 60 fresh out-of-sample trades. Result as printed: mean in-sample performance +38.84%, mean fresh out-of-sample +0.14%, with 49.16% of winners negative out-of-sample. Conclusion as printed: the edge is not generating more strategies, it is rejecting the ones that only look profitable. Attributed in the image to an MIT Laboratory for Financial Engineering quantitative research series, Nov 2025 — that attribution is part of the image claim and is UNVERIFIED (no paper was opened).
engine_training_value: Method, not data: a selection-bias haircut procedure for signal promotion. The simulation output is a labeled null distribution the engine's gate can compare candidate signals against — labels exist by construction.

summary: A coverage-adaptation method: when offenses go condensed and use play-action with deep crossing routes, true split-field Quarters distributions "get caught in a vise" because their built-in rules conflict. The counter is cross-keying the safeties — safeties key across the formation, which lets the corners stay on the top shoulder of their receivers while the safeties act as backstops for the deep crossers. title_or_hook: Statistical Mechanics of Spontaneous Behavior (arXiv:2611.02220, VERIFIED)
summary: A verified preprint: Takahashi & El Hady, "Statistical mechanics of spontaneous behavior" (submitted 1 Nov 2026, cond-mat.stat-mech / biological physics). Its claim, paraphrased from the abstract: how long a behavior *lasts* can by itself explain why a few behaviors fill most of an animal's time — a system that runs until it hits a constraint and then resets spends time in each behavior following a Boltzmann-type law, with the partition function given by the mean time between resets, and bottleneck (critical) states becoming the most occupied. In 47 multi-day fruit-fly recordings, the dominant behavior was only about 13% of bout *starts* but about 49% of total *time*, and its typical duration identified the individual fly.
engine_training_value: A derived feature family: duration-weighted (occupancy) versions of usage stats alongside count-weighted ones, with drive duration as the label-rich quantity. No external dataset needed — play-by-play timestamps/drive data already in nflverse.

author: @benbbaldwin
title_or_hook: nflfastR is changing how EP/EPA is computed: PR #618 values scoring plays net of the opponent's next possession
summary: The most consequential infrastructure post of the run. nflfastR — the EP model underneath nearly every public EPA number, including most of this sweep's football dossiers — is about to change its EP accounting: PR #618 (by guga31bb, opened Nov 5, 2026; 22 comments, 1 review, 9 files, +1213/−73 per the post's link card) values EP on scoring plays net of the opponent's next possession. In plain terms: a touchdown is not worth a flat ~7 minus nothing; the ensuing kickoff hands the opponent a possession with its own expected value, and the new accounting nets that out of the scoring play's value, so EPA on scoring plays (and everything chained to EP) shifts.

The history VERIFIED against OEIS A010060 and the standard literature (Euwe 1929, Proc. KNAW). The sequence is also the "fair-share sequence": balanced alternation (ABBA BAAB...) for dividing contested items when earlier picks are worth more.

summary: "Tools Need Not Speak in Text" (Liu et al., Tsinghua AI Agent Group, Nov 4, 2026): instead of appending raw tool outputs as text, a compressor encodes each observation into continuous latent tokens in the agent's own embedding space, trained with Action-Preserving Training (the agent's next-action distribution under compressed input is aligned to the full-text one). VERIFIED at arXiv and Hugging Face Papers: across four web-search QA benchmarks (NQ, TriviaQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, HotpotQA) and two model families (Qwen, GLM), total token consumption falls 70.01%–89.24% and end-to-end runtime 24.45%–55.97%, with task performance consistently improved. The post's "up to 87.93%" sits inside that range (a specific setting's figure).
engine_training_value: None for the sports engine. For the fleet: a method whose training asset is (observation, action) pairs — the fleet generates those daily, which is the honest path to ever using it.

title_or_hook: PULSE: Bayesian prior-informed RAPM for NBA players
summary: Per the post's own definition (the only source): "PULSE is a Bayesian prior-informed RAPM model, that uses a box score prior and a RAPM lineup update to score NBA players on a points per 100 possessions scale." The architecture is the well-established one: build a box-score-based prior rating per player, then run the RAPM (ridge-regularized lineup regression) update so stint data moves players away from their priors only as evidence accumulates. The family is independently VERIFIED as sound and current: ARC v3 (LumaHoops) is a Bayesian RAPM with the box-score valuation inside the solve as prior, built on 29 seasons; EPM (Dunks & Threes) is the commercial exemplar (statistical plus-minus prior + RAPM). PULSE itself has no paper, site, or

Stated extremes: luckiest DEN +3.3, CHI +2.0, MIN +1.9; unluckiest NYJ −3.1, HOU −1.8, LAC −1.6. summary: A new preprint (Baumann and Starnini) with a precise claim: the collective behavior of a population of LLM agents can be predicted from tests on a single agent, but only if that agent is measured in the context in which it acts; measured out of context, the single-agent test mispredicts what the population does. The author's thread context adds the setup: simulations of 1,000 LLM agents on Erdos–Renyi and Barabasi–Albert networks sharing posts on migration, policing, and gun rights, plus a mean-field theory of the collective behavior.
engine_training_value: None for the sports engine — context only there. For the fleet: an evaluation-design rule (measure in context) that changes how agent performance data gets collected, which is a training-data quality input for every future lane comparison.

summary: A KAIST / DeepAuto.ai paper (Lee, Choi, Baek, Hwang), arXiv:2611.14320 (Nov 10 2026), with a named failure mode and a measured fix. The failure: memory-induced degradation — an agent with memory fails tasks it would solve without memory, because stored lessons bias its decisions (a lesson that is wrong, or a valid lesson misapplied). The fix, Evidence-Linked Memory (implemented as WikiTrace): store each distilled lesson linked to a summary of why its source trajectory succeeded or failed, and to the raw trajectory itself, so the agent can descend to the evidence when lessons conflict. VERIFIED this run at secondary-primary coverage of the paper: 90.2% average across eight test suites vs…

author: @kevin_cole
title_or_hook: Data Debunk: Green Bay's EPA is running ahead of its success rate (Unexpected Points)
summary: A stability argument in the classic EPA-vs-success-rate form: EPA is explosive-sensitive and noisy; success rate is the steadier down-to-down measure. When a team's EPA rank (10th) runs ten places ahead of its success-rate rank (20th) on the back of a league-leading explosive rate (7.9% of plays going 20+), the EPA is borrowing from the least stable play type in football. The method is fully named (opponent-adjusted EPA vs success rate, nflverse data) — the most reproducible dossier in tonight's run.
engine_training_value: The gap itself is the feature: EPA-minus-success divergence per team per week, with explosive rate as a companion, is a trainable regression-risk signal with labels fully owned (future EPA is the outcome it predicts).

author: @run_the_sims
title_or_hook: The Packers paradox: quickest release, deepest passing (two posts)
summary: Covers 2 posts, one dossier. A two-part tendency finding that resolves an apparent contradiction: the quickest release in the league coexists with the deepest passing game because the deep shots are not slow-developing plays — they are quick-game timing throws to two speed receivers who condense half the target tree. The method is a historical ranking (deep-pass yards through 9 games since 2006) plus a target-concentration measure (top-2 WR target rate) plus a timing split (release speed on 0–19-yard throws vs deep volume). The three pieces together are the argument; any one alone would mislead.
engine_training_value: QB release-profile features: deep-pass rate, deep yards share, top-2 target concentration, and (where tracking exists) release time by throw depth — per QB per week, two of four trainable from owned data tonight, the rest named as tracking-label wants.
provenance_json: "timing data credited to @SumerSports. Time-to-throw and air yards live in tracking/NGS-adjacent products; target rates are computable from nflverse."

author: @sfdata9ers
title_or_hook: "Sometimes the best play is throwing it away" — the QB throwaway file (data: FantasyPtsData, min. 135 attempts) — CATCH-UP TARGET
summary: A QB throwaway-rate ranking: throwaways as a share of dropbacks (or attempts), minimum 135 attempts, framed as a skill — the deliberate incompletion that trades a dead play for no sack, no interception risk, and no negative EPA. Throwaway rate is a decision metric, not an accuracy metric: high can mean good pressure management or a QB bailing early; the value is in reading it against pressure and sack numbers, never alone.
engine_training_value: Throwaways per pressured dropback, per QB per week, is a clean label where charted data exists; where it does not, pressure-to-sack rate is the trainable proxy. Name the proxy honestly in the feature store.

author: @The_Coach_A
title_or_hook: Kansas City's double "pick" pressures: two pick concepts on the same play (MatchQuarters)
summary: A pressure-design breakdown: Kansas City (Spagnuolo) running two pick/stunt concepts inside one pressure — the defense's rushers set basketball-style picks on individual protectors so a rusher comes free without outnumbering the protection. The mechanism is assignment confusion by design: each pick isolates one protector (LG drawn by the pop, LT picked by Bolton's path, center occupied across the formation), and the free man is created by geometry, not by sending seven.
engine_training_value: None as data — context only, plainly. The training asset is the scheme taxonomy itself: pressure-package labels (Boss front, pick pressure) that a future film-tagging pass could label, not a metric the engine can train on today.
provenance_json: "full breakdown on MatchQuarters (the author's site, linked in his related posts). This is the third distinct KC pressure package in the corpus this week (AM W10 double-edge simulated pressure, AM W11 slide-protection readout) — the Denver/KC pressure file is becoming a series."

title_or_hook: True Pressure Rate, Week 9: 1,600+ pressures graded by quality; Rousseau still No. 1, Simmons' leap, and the Pressure Quality Ratio
summary: A film-graded pressure metric family, and the grading is the method: raw pressure counts treat a QB's instant escape and a drive-killing hit as the same event, so this product hand-grades every pressure for quality (how much it actually disrupted the play) and builds two outputs — high-quality pressure counts and a Pressure Quality Ratio (quality-weighted pressure production per opportunity, exact denominator on the Substack, not in the post). Simmons' line is the shape of the insight: his raw story since Week 5 is unremarkable, but his high-quality count doubled, which the author surfaces as a breakout the raw totals hide.
engine_training_value: High-quality pressure counts per rusher per week are an external feature family (labels in one analyst's film grading only — stated plainly); the trainable in-house asset is the outcome-weighted pressure proxy, whose labels (sack/throwaway/incompletion outcomes) are owned.

summary: A rigorous introductory algebraic geometry text written to be readable with minimal prerequisites: it builds the algebra-geometry dictionary (varieties on one side, ideals on the other, the Nullstellensatz as the translation theorem) step by step with proofs, examples, and exercises. Algebraic geometry is the mathematics of polynomial systems — the same objects that appear wherever models are polynomial, constraints are varieties, or identifiability questions turn into ideal membership questions.

Poster is a recommender (a repeat source in this corpus — his Oct 29 post delivered the deep-learning theory book that became an ADOPT); the authors and Springer are the origin."

author: @mojunel
title_or_hook: Seven "second brains": GBrain VERIFIED (Garry Tan's agent memory, MIT, ~32.7K stars), six more truncated
summary: The verified head of the list is the find. GBrain is a local-first agent-memory daemon: it stores explicit facts as markdown pages, each carrying its source, supports corrections and withdrawal as first-class operations, organizes pages into a typed knowledge graph, and serves the same memory to any connected agent over MCP — one shared brain across harnesses instead of a memory silo per tool. Its author runs it as his own production memory layer (his stated deployment scale is his claim, carried as such). The other six list entries describe the same design space Garrett's stack already lives in: markdown-native memory, cross-harness resume, nightly self-rule extraction, and one-command Obsidian wiring. The poster is a list-maker and recreator; the origins are…
engine_training_value: None for the prediction engine. For the fleet, a sourced-fact memory with correction semantics is labeled process infrastructure; stated plainly.
provenance_json: "origin repo github.com/garrytan/gbrain (MIT license; TypeScript, runs on Bun; local store is an embedded Postgres via PGLite with vector support). A companion evals repo (garrytan/gbrain-evals) publishes the project's own benchmark reports and defects."

author: @AlexIrrthum
title_or_hook: Scardapane's Alice: a free, friendly, full textbook on the maths of designing neural networks (VERIFIED)
summary: A complete graduate-level primer whose organizing idea (a network is a composition of differentiable primitives, each defined by its input/output signature and its composition rules) is a design grammar, not just a math survey: it teaches how architectures are assembled and why their pieces have the shapes they do. For Garrett's corpus this is the accessible on-ramp volume beside the heavier theory texts already filed (the Petersen & Zech theory book and the Foundations of LLMs volume, both ADOPT in earlier runs).

author: @sfdata9ers
title_or_hook: Short vs. Mid Throwing Accuracy (FantasyPtsData)
summary: A QB accuracy board split by throw depth — short throws against mid-range throws. Depth-split accuracy matters because the two zones test different things: short accuracy is timing and ball placement in structure; mid-range accuracy (the intermediate middle and the intermediate sidelines) is the layer where NFL windows are tightest and where the best QBs separate. A single completion-percentage number hides a QB who is automatic underneath and wild at the intermediate level — exactly the profile that collapses against defenses that take away the short game.

author: @sfdata9ers
title_or_hook: The penalty tax: the Jaguars hurt most by penalties, and offensive TDs negated by penalties (two posts)
summary: Covers 2 posts, one dossier. Two cuts of one ledger: what penalties cost. The first post ranks teams by total penalty harm and names Jacksonville as the league's most-harmed team, with its QB as the face of the cost. The second isolates the most expensive subset: touchdowns actually scored and then erased by a flag. A negated TD is the purest luck/undiscipline unit in the sport — the play succeeded, the points existed, and an infraction (often away from the play) removed them. Tonight's feed independently carries the player-level version of the same file: feed row 71 (@barbour_mike) charts Lawrence as the QB most robbed by penalties and least benefited by them — two sources, one conclusion, same evening.
engine_training_value: Per-team, per-week penalty EPA cost and negated-score counts, fully producible from owned play-by-play with labels in the same data. One of tonight's few finds whose training asset needs no vendor at all.
provenance_json: "Penalty events are public play-by-play data (nflverse carries penalty type, player, and yards on every play); the \"hurt most\" aggregation is the poster's construction. Feed row 71 is inventoried NO-ID."

author: @sfdata9ers
title_or_hook: Which WRs create separation: separation leaderboard, min. 90 routes (FantasyPtsData)
summary: A receiver separation board: how much space a receiver creates from the nearest defender, averaged over routes run, with a 90-route minimum. Separation is a process stat for receivers — it measures the skill (route-running and release) rather than the outcome (targets and catches, which depend on the QB and the scheme). The post's text-level claim is team-shaped: Jets receivers sit at or near the top of the board, which, if the chart bears it out, says the Jets' passing problem is not receiver openness.
engine_training_value: Per-WR separation per week as an external vendor feature; the trainable in-house relatives are targets per route run and yards per route run from owned play-by-play, which the engine can compute today. The vendor label itself stays external.
provenance_json: "Data credited: @FantasyPtsData, minimum 90 routes. Separation at this grain is a tracking-derived or charted vendor metric; the vendor is the source."

author: @sfdata9ers
title_or_hook: Who's sending the house: blitz rate and blitzers per blitz, Weeks 1–9 (FantasyPtsData)
summary: A two-part blitz board: how often each defense blitzes, and when it blitzes, how many rushers it sends. The second number is the payload: a high blitz rate with four-man rushes is a simulated-pressure defense (coverage holds, pressure is manufactured by confusion), while a high rate with five- and six-man rushes is a true send-the-house defense (coverage is thinned and the QB's hot answer exists). Rate alone cannot separate those two defenses; rate crossed with rushers-per-blitz can. The corpus's pressure file has been building exactly this distinction for three days (Denver's simulated menus, Tampa's Hot rotations, Washington's dropped rusher); this board is the league-wide version of it.
engine_training_value: (Defense, week, blitz rate, rushers per blitz) is a labeled feature pair for the matchup layer; labels live in vendor charting (FantasyPtsData) — the standing wanted label, named again. No owned-data substitute exists yet.
provenance_json: "Data credited in the post: @FantasyPtsData, Weeks 1–9. The poster is the compiler of this cut; the underlying blitz charting is the credited vendor's."

author: @sfdata9ers
title_or_hook: Red Zone Defense Rankings
summary: A ranking of defenses inside the red zone. The construction question the title leaves open is the whole dossier: red zone defense measured by TD rate allowed, by points per trip, or by EPA per play gives three different rankings, and they diverge because the red zone is where field position compresses — yards stop mattering and only the end zone counts. A defense can be average between the 20s and elite inside them (short fields neutralize speed and reward power and discipline), and that split is a real, priceable team trait when it persists.
engine_training_value: Red-zone defensive splits (TD rate, points/trip, EPA/play) per week from owned play-by-play; labels fully owned.
provenance_json: "Red zone trips and outcomes are in public play-by-play; the ranking basis is the author's, chart-locked."

author: @boxscorescout
title_or_hook: Most EPA through 85 career games: Mahomes, Rodgers, Allen, Burrow
summary: A career-shape leaderboard: cumulative EPA over each QB's first 85 career games, for QBs who debuted in 1999 or later. Fixing the game count instead of the calendar is the method — it compares QBs at the same career point (85 games is roughly five and a half seasons as a starter), which removes both the longevity advantage and the era-of-debut advantage from a cumulative stat. The top four as stated — Mahomes, Rodgers, Allen, Burrow — mixes two generations, which is the board's argument: early-career EPA production at this level is rare in any era. The account is a returning watchlist name (its expected-points work ran in the Nov 11–12 corpus); this is its first NEW post in two…

author: @sfdata9ers
title_or_hook: Offensive 3rd Down Efficiency: average yards to go vs. conversion rate
summary: A two-axis offensive board: how far a team usually has to go on third down (a measure of what its early downs leave behind) against how often it converts (a measure of third-down execution). The axes separate two different offenses that raw conversion rate merges: a team facing 3rd-and-short all day converts often because its early downs work; a team converting on 3rd-and-long is doing something harder and less sustainable. The honest third-down stat is conversion rate conditioned on distance, and plotting the two axes side by side is the conditioning made visible.
engine_training_value: Third-down distance distribution and distance-conditioned conversion above expectation, per offense per week — fully owned labels, a direct feature family.
provenance_json: "Every input (down, distance, conversion) is in public play-by-play; the poster is the compiler."

author: @vintcessun
title_or_hook: Skillware: agents should select verified capability modules, not improvise code (arXiv:2611.07652) — VERIFIED
summary: Skillware is an architectural standard for packaging agent capabilities as software: each capability bundle combines a typed JSON input contract, a deterministic Python implementation, task directives, bundled data, and automated unit tests, versioned as one unit. In-process adapters translate a bundle into whatever tool format the host model expects, so the model does planning and selection while tested code does execution — and because execution is deterministic code rather than generated text, the permission boundary is auditable. The paper behind the post is verified: "Don't Prompt Your Agents. Equip Them" (arXiv:2611.07652), which reports evaluating 23 frontier and open-weight models across 368 benchmark conditions, with small local models (3B–8B) equipped with Skillware outperforming unequipped frontier models on complex multi-step workflows.
engine_training_value: None directly — fleet infrastructure, not engine data. Indirectly: deterministic, tested collectors produce cleaner labeled data for the engine than improvised scripts do; the gain is data quality, stated as such.
provenance_json: "Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07652 (Vladimiros Peilivanidis, ARPA Hellenic Logical Systems, submitted 5 Nov 2026, 51 pages). Code: github.com/arpahls/skillware; the package is on PyPI as skillware; project site skillware.site."
